chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtari, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When there remains upon him something from the dower, and he knows that she has a husband, then whatever she has taken is for her due to what she has permitted of her private parts, and he shall withhold from her whatever remains with him.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the remaining dower if a woman has another husband?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the financial rights in a marriage contract when the wife has not yet received the full dower (mahr), establishing that the portion already paid is considered her due in exchange for the permissibility of conjugal relations (istihlal al-farj). Consequently, the husband retains the unpaid balance, a ruling that underscores the contractual nature of mahr as compensation for marital intimacy in Shia jurisprudence. This principle is frequently cited by scholars like Al-Shaykh al-Mufid and Al-Tusi to resolve disputes regarding partial payment and the wife's right to withhold intimacy until the remainder is settled.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hafs Bin Al Bakhtary, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When there remains upon him something from the dower, and he comes to know that for her is a husband, so whatever she has taken so it is for her due to what she has permitted from her private parts, and he would withhold from her whatever remains with him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hafs ibn al-Bakhtariy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If something of mahr (dower) remains due on him and he learns that she has a husband, then what she has received belongs to her because of its making his going to bed with her lawful and he can withhold the remaining of mahr (dower).”’
